newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Jurys CEO says expects strong profits in '96.
newsitem.headline: Jurys CEO says expects strong profits in '96.

text.p: Jurys Hotel Group chief executive Peter Malone said on Monday that he expected a good performance for the hotel chain in 1996.

"Overall profits should be very good. I hope the share price remains strong. It has been very strong for the past year and it will probably translate into strong profits at year end," Malone told reporters after an annual shareholders meeting.
Jurys' share price was trading at 280 pence, up 55 pence since the beginning of the year.

The share price was hit by concerns that tourism numbers would slump after Northern Ireland's pro-nationalist Irish Republican Army (IRA) ended an 18-month ceasefire with a bomb blast in London's Canary Wharf in February.
Jurys shares, which had moved back up to a high of 285 on July 4, took another dive after a Northern Ireland hotel, based in Enniskillen, was bombed in fresh sectarian violence.
Malone told reporters that the collapse of the IRA ceasefire had not affected overall business and that company projections for the rest of the year were positive.
He said he looked forward to a busy few months ahead when the Irish EU presidency reaches its climax and attracts more EU officials and media personnel to Ireland.
Ireland took on the mantle of European Union President in July, 1996, a role it will play for six months.

"The EU Presidency gets into full swing from September onwards and we expect a very busy Autumn and Winter in Dublin. The new Jurys Customs House Inn will open on schedule next Monday, September 2, so Jurys will have three Dublin hotels to cater for the extra European visitors," he said.
